summary.text: Seth Bodnar is an independent candidate for the open U.S. Senate seat. A West Point graduate, Rhodes Scholar and Army Special Forces officer, he became a General Electric executive and then served as president of the University of Montana from 2018 until he resigned in January 2026. He entered the race on March 4, 2026, running as an independent who says he will not caucus with either party.

paragraphs.text: Raised in Franklin, Pennsylvania, the son of two public school teachers.

Graduated first in his class from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point with a bachelor's degree in economics, then studied at Hertford College, Oxford, as a Rhodes Scholar and Truman Scholar, earning two master's degrees.

Served in the U.S. Army as an infantry officer in the 101st Airborne Division, deployed to Iraq, and served as a Green Beret in the 1st Special Forces Group, commanding a detachment; he later taught economics at West Point. He remained a lieutenant colonel in the Montana Army National Guard as of 2022.
Joined General Electric in 2011 and became a senior executive in its transportation division, including as chief digital officer.

Became the 19th president of the University of Montana in January 2018. According to his campaign, enrollment was turned around, finances stabilized and research output doubled; the university also settled a sex-discrimination lawsuit for $350,000 in 2024 that named him, according to Wikipedia.
Resigned as university president in January 2026 and announced his Senate run on March 4, 2026. Wikipedia reports he was last registered with a party in 2012, as a Democrat.
According to his campaign, his wife is a pediatrician and they are raising three children; Wikipedia lists the family's residence as Missoula.
